newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak parliament rejects new penal code.
newsitem.headline: Slovak parliament rejects new penal code.

text.p: Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's ruling coalition government suffered its first parliamentary defeat on Tuesday when parliament rejected a controversial new penal code.

The law was rejected by 67 votes against to 69 in favour with four abstentions and two non-voters among the 142 deputies present. A majority of 72 votes in favour would have been needed to pass the law.

The penal code was the second version of a law sent back to parliament for review by President Michal Kovac, who came to parliament to explain why he had refused to sign either law. The draft will not be discussed further.

According to the law, sharply criticised by the United States, the European Union and human rights organisations, activities such as organising anti-government demonstrations or slandering the republic abroad would be punishable offences.
"The law named offences against the republic which even communist legislature did not need," Kovac told parliament.

Deputies of Meciar's Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) and of junior coalition partner, the Slovak National Party, voted in favour of the law, while those of the other coalition partner, the ultra left Workers' Party, voted against.
